title: A vote in the Security Council
body: A fictional draft resolution calls for an immediate ceasefire in a region where thousands of civilians have been displaced by fighting. When the Security Council votes, fourteen of its fifteen members, including four of the permanent members and all ten non-permanent members, vote in favour. One permanent member votes against the resolution, saying it would harm the security of a close ally. After the meeting, the ambassador of a small country tells reporters that the system is unfair: 'One country has set aside the wishes of fourteen. Many of us believe this privilege conflicts with democracy and the sovereign equality of states.' A senior diplomat from another country replies that, however unfair it may look, the privilege should be kept for now, because the world body needs the continued support and involvement of the great powers to be effective.
